form.label: Network evidence
form.description: Whether a permitted flow to a listening port has ever actually been observed, and where the app refuses to say.

div.span: A firewall logs a flow that happened. A permitted rule nobody has used yet produces no log line at all, so this evidence under-reports by construction: a port that reads not observed may simply be one nobody has tried. This page never lowers a finding's priority, and missing firewall data costs a finding confidence, never its place in the queue.

panel.title: What the firewall evidence says about the fleet

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_netevidence_lookup | search hostname=$host_filter|s$ | stats count BY observed_grade | eval rk_order = case(observed_grade=="confirmed observed", 0, observed_grade=="historically observed", 1, observed_grade=="not observed", 2, 1=1, 3) | sort rk_order | fields observed_grade, count

viz.option: The assess job has not run, or it found no open finding on a listening port. Nothing here is a statement about your network.

panel.title: Can this evidence say anything at all?

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_netevidence_lookup | search hostname=$host_filter|s$ | stats count AS "Host and port rows", dc(hostname) AS Hosts BY coverage_state | rename coverage_state AS "Coverage state" | eval "What it means" = case( 'Coverage state'=="no firewall data", "No edges reached the app. Every row is unknown, and correctly so.", 'Coverage state'=="no entry point declared", "Edges exist, but nothing declares where an attacker starts, so no absence means anything.", 'Coverage state'=="firewall data stale", "The newest edge is older than the freshness window, so silence is about the feed, not the network.", 'Coverage state'=="host not in graph", "No edge resolved to this host, so the app cannot claim it is visible to the firewall.", 'Coverage state'=="covered", "The host resolved to at least one edge, so a silent port is evidence about the port.", 1=1, "") | table "Coverage state", "Host and port rows", Hosts, "What it means"

| inputlookup riskability_netevidence_lookup | search hostname=$host_filter|s$ $grade_filter$ | eval rk_order = case(observed_grade=="confirmed observed", 0, observed_grade=="historically observed", 1, observed_grade=="not observed", 2, 1=1, 3) | eval "Last edge" = if(isnotnull(edge_last_seen) AND edge_last_seen!="", strftime(tonumber(edge_last_seen), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M"), "never") | eval Sources = if(n_srcs > 0, srcs_text . " (" . n_srcs . ")", "") | sort rk_order, hostname, port | rename hostname AS Host, port AS Port, protocols_text AS Protocol, observed_grade AS Grade, observed_reason AS Why, entry_text AS "Entry point", entry_pressure AS Pressure, sessions AS Sessions | table Host, Port, Protocol, Grade, "Entry point", Pressure, Sources, Sessions, "Last edge", Why

panel.title: Where the app refused to name a host

div.b: An address is only a host's for as long as something observed it holding one.
div.span: These rows had a permitted flow to an address the inventory could not tie to exactly one machine at the moment it was logged, so the flow is reported and deliberately not attributed. Refusing is the safe wrong answer: a false attribution invents an attack path that nobody can find and everybody has to chase.

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_netevidence_lookup | search hostname=$host_filter|s$ | where identity_state!="resolved" | stats count AS Rows, values(hostname) AS Hosts BY identity_state | eval "What it means" = case( identity_state=="shared", "More than one host has held this address, so a flow to it belongs to no one host.", identity_state=="stale", "The address claim does not cover the moment the flow was logged.", identity_state=="outside estate", "No host in the inventory has ever been seen holding this address. Expected for an internet entry point.", identity_state=="malformed address", "The firewall record's destination could not be parsed as an address.", identity_state=="no edge to resolve", "No permitted flow reached this host and port, so there was nothing to attribute.", 1=1, "") | eval Hosts = mvjoin(mvdedup(Hosts), " ") | rename identity_state AS "Identity" | sort - Rows | table Identity, Rows, "What it means", Hosts

panel.title: Address coverage, and whether the collector could report it

div.b: No row for a host means never assessed, not "holds no addresses".
div.span: A host showing zero addresses may sit on a segment nothing logs, or every one of its listeners may bind a wildcard, which the bind-derived source cannot see at all. Those look identical here and are completely different facts, and only the second is a limit of this app rather than of the site. The collector and schema columns answer the "could it even have reported them" half.

search.query: | inputlookup riskability_hostaddr_hoststate_lookup | search hostname=$host_filter|s$ | eval "Identity stable" = if(contested_addresses > 0, "no, " . contested_addresses . " address(es) claimed by another host", "yes") | rename hostname AS Host, addresses AS Addresses, ipv4_addresses AS IPv4, ipv6_addresses AS IPv6, addr_source AS Source, swinv_version AS "Collector", schema_version AS Schema | sort - Addresses, Host | table Host, Addresses, IPv4, IPv6, "Identity stable", Source, Collector, Schema

div.b: Two macros, both shipped resolving to nothing.
div.span: With neither wired, every row reads unknown, which is the correct answer when no firewall data has arrived.

ul.li: riskability_fw_edges — reduce your firewall index to unique permitted edges: src_ip, dest_ip, port, protocol, sessions, edge_first_seen, edge_last_seen.

riskability_fw_entry_points — declare where an attacker plausibly starts: entry_cidr, entry_name, entry_scan_pressure. Only a constant pressure entry point can ever produce a not observed grade, because only there does the absence of a flow mean anything.

div.span: A range matches on containment alone, so declaring 0.0.0.0/0 as the internet also matches every private address and will report internal traffic as arriving from outside. List the ranges that actually face the boundary. The reasoning, the failure directions and what this is deliberately not are in docs/ROUTE-EVIDENCE.md.
